blocks.text: 1. Graph Construction

blocks.alt: Triples combine into a connected graph

blocks.text: Relation Extraction closed by showing entity and relation extraction together producing exactly what graph construction needs. Graph Construction, assembling extracted entities and relations into one queryable graph, is the step that actually turns those triples into a usable structure.
It inserts each confirmed triple as nodes and an edge into a persistent graph store.
2. From Individual Triples To A Connected Graph
As covered generally in Relation Extraction, each individual triple is just one isolated fact on its own.
Graph construction inserts many such triples so they connect into one navigable structure.

blocks.text: 3. Deduplicating Entities During Insertion

blocks.alt: A new entity is checked for already existing, then merged if so

blocks.text: As with entity resolution across sources in Knowledge Graph RAG, inserting a triple whose entity already exists must reuse the existing node, not create a duplicate.
Construction is where entity resolution actually gets applied, not just decided in theory.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Inserting a new triple mentioning Falcon Cloud must check whether a Falcon Cloud node already exists in the graph and reuse it, rather than silently creating a second, disconnected node for the same real entity.

blocks.text: 4. Validating Triples Against The Schema

blocks.alt: A triple goes through schema validation to check if valid

blocks.text: As with a schema constraining what can be expressed in Knowledge Graphs, a triple naming an entity type or relationship type outside the schema should be rejected at insertion.
This keeps the graph consistent with the rules defined ahead of time.
5. Incremental Versus Batch Construction

blocks.alt: Incremental construction one at a time is compared against batch construction all at once

blocks.text: A batch build processes a whole document set at once, while incremental construction adds new triples as new documents arrive.
Both approaches insert the same kind of validated, deduplicated triples.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","When triples are inserted"],"rows":[["Batch construction","Whole document set processed at once"],["Incremental construction","New triples added as new documents arrive"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Choosing A Graph Storage Backend

blocks.alt: Neo4j is compared against other graph database options

blocks.text: As with querying graph databases with structured queries in Knowledge Graph RAG, the constructed graph needs to live somewhere queryable, typically a dedicated graph database.
Construction is not complete until the graph is actually stored somewhere retrieval can reach.
7. Conflicting Triples Need A Resolution Rule

blocks.alt: Triple A conflicts with triple B

blocks.text: Two extracted triples can occasionally contradict each other, such as conflicting values for the same relationship.
Construction needs an explicit rule for which one wins, rather than silently keeping both.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Two source documents claiming different headquarters cities for the same company need an explicit resolution rule, such as preferring the most recent source, rather than the graph silently storing both contradictory facts.

blocks.text: 8. Graph Quality Depends On Upstream Extraction
As with incorrect relations corrupting traversal in Relation Extraction, construction can only insert what entity and relation extraction actually handed it.
A well built graph still inherits every upstream extraction error unchanged.
9. Recognizing When Careful Graph Construction Is Worth The Added Rigor

blocks.alt: The graph being used for critical decisions points toward investing in careful construction

blocks.text: A graph meant to grow continuously from new documents needs disciplined construction.
A small, one-time, hand-checked graph, by contrast, can tolerate a simpler construction process.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Inserting a triple for an entity that already exists as a fresh, duplicate node.
Skipping schema validation and letting out-of-schema entity or relation types into the graph.
Having no explicit rule for which of two contradictory triples should win.
Assuming careful construction can fix errors that already exist in the extracted triples.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Graph construction assembles extracted entities and relations into one queryable graph.
It inserts many individual triples so they connect into one navigable structure.
Inserting a triple whose entity already exists must reuse the existing node, not duplicate it.
Triples naming out-of-schema entity or relationship types should be rejected at insertion.
Batch construction processes a whole document set at once; incremental construction adds triples over time.
The constructed graph needs to live in a queryable store, typically a dedicated graph database.
Contradictory triples need an explicit resolution rule, not silent storage of both.
A well built graph still inherits every error already present in its upstream extraction.
